newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm on options expiry, new spec.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm on options expiry, new spec.

text.p: IPE prompt gas oil extended a late rally shortly before the close on Thursday.
Buyers moved in strongly on the front month ahead of today's options expiry, while next week's Sept contract expiry also was seen as supportive.
Many buyers, and one Wall Street trader in particular, were expecting a shortage of 0.2 percent sulphur gas oil to cover deliveries to the screen.
Sept gas oil closed up $5.25 at $213, Oct closed up $1.50, widening the Sep/Oct backwardation to $9 a tonne.
The European gas oil pool, currently 0.2 percent sulphur for both heating oil and diesel, will be split 60:40 into 0.2 percent for heating oil and 0.05 poercent for diesel from October 1.
The IPE contract will continue to specify only 0.2 percent.
"We're thinking if stocks are turned around enough we might be seeing a physical shortage (of 0.2 percent)" said one broker.
Oct Brent was eight cents down at $22.04 a barrel by 1703 GMT, in the middle of the session trading range.
Brent was helped off lows at $21.75 by a strong performance on NYMEX products.--London Newsroom +44 171 542 5387
